thread:
Maya: Thought experiment: what if we express routing decisions as a tiny policy language instead of scattered flags? Could simplify cross-hosting semantics.
Jonah: Agree. Right now behavior is implicit in code paths. A policy DSL would make precedence explicit and testable.
Priya: Example idea:
```
route_policy "customer-default" {
  prefer: [private, dedicated, hosted]
  constraints: {
    data_residency: "local-only"
    max_latency_ms: 120
  }
  fallbacks: ["shared-cache-only"]
}
```
Sree: Nice. Having named policies lets us bind them to tenants and to rollout gates. Also helps audit.
Devon: We should be careful: DSL should be purely declarative and not include enforcement code. Runtime reads policy and applies precedence rules (pin > policy > hint).
Maya: How do we handle version pinning? If tenant pins model v2 to a private pool, policy must not override.
Jonah: Pinning is a high-priority constraint in the runtime: policy can only relax, not strengthen, residency. We'll document as: pin supersedes policy.
Priya: Telemetry needs to show which policy evaluated and which constraint caused final decision. Add fields: policy_id, decision_reason, decision_path.
Sree: Example decision_path: `["policy:private-favored","probe:dedicated-checked(30ms)","selected:private-v2"]` Good for debug and SLO attribution.
Maya: Rollouts: we want to express weighted routing in the same DSL so canary + can fall back automatically. Something like: `variants: [{v1: 90},{v2:10}]` with rollout rules.
Devon: For safety, add a circuit-breaker annotation on policy: `max_probe_rate_per_minute` and `sticky_fallback_minutes`. Prevents probe storms and oscillation.
Jonah: Ops question: how do we push policy changes? Config service with change streams and an op-audit. Changes should carry a dry-run mode for X% traffic before flip.
Priya: Add `dry_run: {pct: 5, duration_min: 60}` to policy. Runtime records dry_run_decision but ignores it for enforcement.
Sree: Security: policy evaluation must never cause plaintext prompt to move to a host without appropriate KMS. So policy should include `allowed_kms: [kms-id]` and runtime checks that before routing.
Maya: Good call. Also need a clear rollback hook: when policy update fails canary, we must auto-revert to previous policy and emit an incident.
Jonah: Implementation notes: policy compiler produces a compact instruction set the runtime can evaluate quickly. Keep parity across hosted/dedicated/private agents.
Devon: Tests: unit tests for precedence table, integration test simulating 10k reqs with tails and verifying sticky fallback and probe rate limits.
Priya: For observability, add a marker `policy_eval_id` to traces so we can join logs to the config change that produced them.
Sree: UX: Console should show policy simulation overlay on traffic graph and let SEs preview where traffic would route under new policy.
Maya: Who takes the RFC? I can sketch DSL + precedence table. Jonah will add migration plan for existing flags to DSL.
Devon: I'll add runtime constraints (probe guard, kms check) and tests.
ops-bot: RFC draft opened: https://go/repo/pulls/4092 title: "Policy-driven routing for hosting abstractions"
Jonah: Great. Let's avoid adding rich semantics into policy for now (no arbitrary hooks). Keep it small and review after one sprint.
Priya: I'll make a short prototype of the telemetry annotations in the next infra sprint.
Maya: Thanks all. We'll iterate in the RFC. :wave:
